current.text: Rookie. Brooklyn drafted him sixth overall in the 2026 draft.
Projected starting point guard for Brooklyn. Josh is about 80% sure he will start.
Josh does not know when Brown will be available to play.
Late-round flyer at best. Josh projects him at 150 to 180 in both formats, worth a pick in rounds 10 to 13. He took Brown late in a mock draft and regretted it because his availability is unclear.
Expected to struggle early, with terrible turnovers and poor efficiency. He will probably be bad until around February. If you draft him and he starts, hold him until about Thanksgiving.
Probably Brooklyn's third usage option. He could average about 5 assists and over 1 steal in 29 to 30 minutes.
Julius Randle is expected to handle the ball a lot. Coach Jordi Fernandez wants several ball handlers rather than one traditional point guard.

Brooklyn is projected to win about 28 games. It does not own its draft pick (Houston does), so it has no reason to tank. It is running a development season, and the second half could bring more minutes for young players like Brown. Michael Porter Jr. is a trade candidate.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league. With a March 28 end, its playoff schedule is 3-4-3 games (10 total) with one back-to-back.

durable.text: Very talented point guard. He can dribble, pass and shoot, has unlimited range, dynamic athleticism and good length at 6'4 or 6'5. He has strong passing vision. The Nets see upside on defense.

High-usage guard at Louisville. He shot many threes, posted good assist and steal rates and shot free throws very well. He turned it over more than three times per game, and poor shot selection hurt his efficiency from the field and from three.
Expected to hurt FG% and turnovers. His projected FG% is the weakest part of his category profile.
Had a back injury before the draft. Experts do not see it as a concern.

note: Both sites price him at 0 USD and rank him 155 (Yahoo) and 198 (ESPN). Josh's 150 to 180 projection also falls outside our 144-player pool, so he is a 1 USD final pick at most and more likely a waiver target. His projected 41.6% FG on 10 to 13 attempts and about 2 turnovers make him a drag early, and nobody knows yet when he will be available. Watch whether he starts at point guard and how much he plays by Thanksgiving. His value should come in the second half, when Brooklyn may give its young players more minutes.
